newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian domestic credits 2.3 pct down in April.
newsitem.headline: Romanian domestic credits 2.3 pct down in April.

text.p: Romania's internal credits slipped by 2.3 percent to 39.4 trillion lei at end-April after a 3.8 percent slide the previous month, central bank data (BNR) showed on Tuesday.

Net credits to the Romanian government fell by 9.3 percent to 4.7 trillion lei in April as the State Treasury General Account swiched to a 789.5 billion lei surplus after a 191.5 billion deficit at end-March.
Local economists say the recovery of the state treasury account was a result of seasonal factors as budget revenues surged after payments of 1996 profit tax due in April.
With banks' lending rates on the rise, non-government credits continued a downward trend in April but their 1.3 percent fall was lower than a 6.1 percent drop in March.
Banks' average lending rates for non-bank customers rose to an annual 112.7 percent in April from 108 percent the previous month, BNR data showed.
Hard currency credits inched down to 18.22 trillion lei in April from 18.5 trillion in March, when they saw a 11 percent decline. They took about 53 percent of end-April non-government loans.
Leu credits fell slightly to 16.41 trillion lei in April from 16.58 trillion the previous month, with loans to state companies dipping by 2.7 percent to 8.8 trillion.
Credits to private firms went up by 2.3 percent to 6.79 trillion lei in April when short-term loans accounted for 80 percent of total leu loans.
